coherence.reasons: Both documents run the same logical line: enter via Amazon, retail-led fails the board's limits, payback hinges on ACoS, restate the ambition, gate retail. X's governing thought, five-point summary and slide titles map one-to-one, and its seven-condition test of the CEO hypothesis ties each verdict to evidence and to the revised answer. Its gates use thresholds derived from its own model (28.6% hurdle, 300k units, >20% awareness band). Minor flaws in X: summary point 4 packs two ideas together (ad-cost risk and the $40M shortfall), and slide 4's title leans on a '1% share' line that the rest of the argument does not need. Y is clean and well sectioned, and its summary also follows the slides. But its close is slightly less consistent: it positions $40M as something 'a gated retail phase 2 must earn' after showing that retail fixed costs sink the economics, and resolves this only in a one-line note that phase 2 'needs its own case'. Its guardrails list thresholds without consequences, so the 'gated' claim in the governing thought is less fully supported.

judgment.reasons: Both reach the key's preferred recommendation (Amazon-led, gated, ambition reset, retail deferred) and both reject Option B on the cap, payback and margin floor. X weighs the alternatives and trade-offs more fully. It quantifies what choosing the US over Japan costs ($1.8M of Japan cash forgone, $4.1M against the 32% ACoS case) and what it buys. It sets out the board's real choice between re-phasing the ambition and relaxing the guardrails. It sizes a $4M funding envelope against the combined downside. Its gates carry explicit if-met and if-missed actions, including scale-back or exit with the loss capped at about $2.4–3.7M. It also sizes the stall case that two of three Amazon-first peers suffered. Y states the same 28.6% hurdle and five guardrails, but does not say what happens if ACoS breaches it; that leaves 'what would trigger a change' weak. Its Japan treatment is one table row plus 'remains an option'. Its retail gate keeps the CEO's $10M threshold without testing whether a retail phase could fit the guardrails even at 20% awareness.

evidence.reasons: Both get the required calculations right: unit contributions ($10.72/$4.01–4.72 Amazon, $7.54 retail), B peak of −$20.8M, 4.5% group margin in 2027, A cumulative cash of +2.4/+0.4/−2.3 at 25/28/32% ACoS, break-even 28.6% (26.9% with the tariff), and K-beauty growth. Both handle the $5.2B figure, the units-per-door benchmark against Onsoo's 4–9% awareness, the 4.0 delisting bar, the correlation-is-not-causation point and the survivorship in Amazon-first peers. X uses the critical evidence more deeply. It adds a sell-through × halo grid showing B fails payback in every cell, a halo break-even (1.6× to fit the cap, 3.1× to pay back), a stall case, a volume −20% case, FX, combined ACoS-and-duty cases, and a model of the CEO's 2029 retail step. It also flags that pilot growth is slowing and lists its modelling choices. X's slips are small: the '1% of the market' sizing line, an extrapolated 333k run-rate (caveated), and an illustrative 2032 extension (labelled as such). Y's bridge and break-even formula are transparent and correct, but it tests fewer sensitivities. It also says Korea's 48% repeat 'shows the headroom', which leans toward the Korean-repeat trap, and implies Mooncrest was removed by the same retailer review, which the pack does not state.

revision.reasons: Both keep the CEO's Amazon-first launch with conditions and both raise the retail awareness trigger from 15% to 20% using Table 8 against the 4.0 delisting bar. That matches the expected 'keep with conditions'. X is more explicit and more thorough. It breaks the hypothesis into seven testable conditions with HOLDS / AT RISK / FAILS verdicts. It keeps the launch, marks payback as at risk, and models the CEO's 2029 national retail step: group margin 6.0% and cumulative cash −$13.8M even at 4.6 units per door. From that it concludes the trigger must also require a cheaper retail format that fits the guardrails, plus Amazon revenue of at least $20M. It also re-phases the $40M target. Y updates the awareness gate and restates the ambition but keeps the $10M sales trigger untested. It notes only briefly that retail phase 2 'needs its own case', without showing that the second half of the hypothesis as stated would breach the margin floor.

overall.reasons: Both documents give the board a correct, defensible answer with accurate numbers and avoid the main traps. X would serve the decision maker better. It makes the trade-offs decision-ready: ambition against guardrails, and the US against Japan with the opportunity cost quantified. It bounds the downside with stall, combined ACoS-and-tariff and 38% ACoS cases. It turns the payback risk into gates with explicit thresholds, consequences and an exit path. It also shows why the CEO's 2029 retail step would itself breach the margin floor. Y is shorter and clearer in places, notably the break-even ACoS derivation and the retail bridge. But it leaves the gates without consequences, treats Japan thinly, and does not test the second half of the CEO's hypothesis.
